system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: A live command toggles extension state, and before_agent_start rewrites the system prompt on the next turn.
system_prompt_style.note: Extension hook can recompose system prompt at runtime; skills also selected from descriptions.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: One editor for prompts, @ file references, and ! shell commands, with steering you can type while the agent works.
env_context_strategy.note: Native grep/glob in crates/atomic-natives/src/grep.rs suggests search tools; tool list not in evidence.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Compaction deletes low-value transcript lines without rewriting what survives; <keepContext> pins exact text.
context_compaction.note: Verbatim line-deletion compaction; closest value summarize (heuristic span reduction). Mechanism not seen in code.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Atomic walking its own session JSONL one event per line, showing each event's type, id, and parent id

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Atomic can run tool-capable models exposed through llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, SGLang, Hugging Face, or a compatible OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google endpoint.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Edits are anchored to a 4-hex snapshot tag, so a file that changed behind the model's back fails loudly instead of being overwritten.
edit_primitive.note: Hashline edits (line anchored by hash); closest value line_range_edit. Other edit ops not in evidence.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Use /workflow <name> key=value to validate static inputs against TypeBox before a run starts.
tool_schema_source.note: TypeBox schemas imply code-derived schemas; MCP servers supported.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Atomic connects through installed CLIs, MCP servers, APIs, scripts, and custom extensions; you supply the credentials and permissions.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Executable checks and fresh reviewers produce evidence; failures route into bounded repair until the gate passes.
loop_primitives.note: Default chat is an agent loop; workflows (opt-in) add staged pipelines and repair loops.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Plans are durable files under .atomic/todos/: plain text you can grep, review, and commit alongside the code.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Use direct chat for small, interactive work. Use a skill or bounded subagent when the parent should stay in control.
multi_agent_topology.note: Subagents (nine bundled) and intercom peers reachable; orchestrator_workers when used.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Fan work out to scoped subagents that do the reading, so the main context stays small.
delegation_mechanism.note: Also intercom message passing between sessions.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Put an approval gate anywhere in the graph and the run waits for a person before it proceeds.
human_in_loop.note: Per-call permission via shipped permission-gate extension (opt-in); default has no gate.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Plans are durable files under .atomic/todos/: plain text you can grep, review, and commit alongside the code.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: A SKILL.md file teaches the agent a procedure it loads on demand - the same format Claude Code and Codex use.
long_term_memory.note: file_notes via research/ documents and todos persisted in repo.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Runs checkpoint as they go, so killing the process leaves them retained and resumable instead of lost.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Executable checks and fresh reviewers produce evidence; failures route into bounded repair until the gate passes.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Use direct chat for small, interactive work.

rollback.evidence_quote: Parallel agents each get their own git worktree, so concurrent edits cannot collide.
rollback.note: Session fork/tree also allows conversation branching.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: Iterates with a durable ledger until explicit completion evidence or bound exhaustion.
termination_condition.note: Workflow iteration bounds imply max_steps in workflows; caps not evidenced in code.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: Atomic has no built-in sandbox or command-level shell permission gate. Tools and extensions run with your user permissions.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Tools and extensions run with your user permissions.

network_policy.evidence_quote: Atomic has no built-in sandbox or command-level shell permission gate.

permission_model.evidence_quote: Atomic has no built-in sandbox or command-level shell permission gate.
permission_model.note: Opt-in tool_call hook extensions can prompt or block.

tracing.evidence_quote: Every session is an append-only JSONL file on disk, so you can grep it, diff it, and script against it.

replayability.evidence_quote: Fork a session at any point and try a second approach without losing the first

guardrails.evidence_quote: A tool-call hook inspects the arguments and rejects the call before it ever reaches your shell.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Atomic’s primitives are built for the software engineering lifecycle.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Atomic can run tool-capable models exposed through llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, SGLang, Hugging Face, or a compatible OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google endpoint.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: Atomic is a fork of Pi, so it works with the providers, tools, MCP servers, skills, and extensions already in your Pi stack.
